title: VIDEO: Bay Village police look for suspects in theft ring targeting local Walgreens - NewsBreak
text:
By Jack Shea ,
2 hours ago
BAY VILLAGE, Ohio (WJW) – Bay Village police said they are trying to identify members of a gang of thieves who have been targeting a Walgreens store in the West Shore community.
BVPD Detective Sgt. Jay Elish shared surveillance video with FOX 8 of one of the crimes committed on Oct. 12.
“This is one of the females in October, walking into the Walgreens,” he said. “You notice she has a bag over her shoulder and she’s wearing a surgical mask. And here are two more with the group, a male and a female walking in, the female had an oversized bag.”
Former coach sentenced for felony sexual battery against Hawken Upper School student Investigators said the three people caught on video were posing as customers at the Walgreens on Wolf Road, but they are actually part of an organized theft ring that has struck at Walgreens across Northeast Ohio.
The professional shoplifters have hit the Walgreens in Bay Village three times: once in September, then again in October and again in November.
“They’re in and out within five minutes and they’re going in with a bag that they intend to fill up and they’re running out the door,” Elish said.
Police said members of the ring are going after hygiene and beauty products that they stuff into oversized bags before making their getaway in cars that include a Kia sedan with an obscured temporary license tag and a suspected rental car with Colorado plates.
“It appears they are going after high-dollar products, you know, items that cost a little bit more than the average hygiene product, but they are stealing in volume,” said Elish.
Based on the large amount of merchandise taken from the store in Bay Village and other Walgreens around the region, authorities believe that members of the ring are filling what amounts to a shopping list.
“They generally are doing it so they can provide those products to someone else. Someone asks them to go steal them and they may show up in another store somewhere else or they may be sold or traded on the street, almost like a laundry list of items,” said Elish.
Could pasta prices go up? Cleveland restaurant reacts Investigators said during the three trips to the Walgreens in Bay Village, members of the ring took more than $5,000 worth of products.
Police said there is a good reason that they have placed a priority on tracking down the members of the group of thieves and stopping their wholesale shoplifting.
“The loss to these larger corporate stores gets passed on to us, the consumers, and that contributes to the increase in prices everywhere. If we can deter people from coming in and stealing in large volume, it can possibly help keep the prices of products down,” said Elish.
Investigators said Walgreens issued an alert about the theft ring that was sent to employees at stores across the region.
Anyone with information about members of the group is asked to call Bay Village police at 440-871-1234.
